## What this notebook did not do

Where a step needed a package, model or genome resource this environment does not ship, the cell said so and continued. An existing message means that step did not run — do not read its absence as a clean result.

Next steps that belong elsewhere:

- **Raw reads to fragments** — alignment and Cell Ranger ATAC / cellranger-atac count produce the fragments.tsv.gz or BAM; they are wrappers, not notebook cells. This notebook starts from fragments, a BAM, a saved .h5ad or a 10x peak matrix.
- **Genome FASTA and gene annotation** — snapatac2 bundles chrom_sizes for hg38/mm10/hg19/mm39 offline, but the gene annotation (GFF3, ~50 MB) and FASTA (~845 MB) are lazy downloads from a slow host. TSSe, gene activity and motif enrichment need them: pass gene_anno / genome_fasta as local files, or let snapatac2 download once into its cache. Without them those cells report the gap and continue.
- **chromVAR / ArchR / Signac** — chromVAR deviation scores and the R/Bioconductor scATAC route are not in this pure-conda Python environment. The TF layer here is snapatac2 motif_enrichment plus a TF-gene regulatory network; for chromVAR use a project environment (R ArchR/Signac or pip chromVAR).
- **episcanpy** — episcanpy 0.4.0 imports numpy.NaN, removed in numpy 2.x which snapatac2/scanpy 1.12 require; it cannot coexist and is reported as a gap, not installed.
- **Bulk ChIP-seq / CUT&Tag** — peak-centric bulk chromatin profiling is the sibling chromatin-profiling plugin (R/Bioconductor, pure downstream), not this single-cell plugin.
attribution: Analysis structure and teaching text are an original distillation of the snapatac2 documentation and tutorials (Zhang et al., MIT license) — https://github.com/kaizhang/SnapATAC2, with single-cell best practices (Apache 2.0). The code is original to this plugin and runs in the private plugin:scatac environment (snapatac2 2.10 + scanpy 1.12 + MACS3 3.1): no install cells, no Colab paths, and the config cell is the single place to tune parameters.

genome.comment: bundled chrom_sizes genome: hg38, mm10, hg19, mm39; for another genome pass chrom_sizes. chrom_sizes is offline; annotation/FASTA are not

chrom_sizes.comment: two-column chrom<TAB>size file for a non-bundled genome (input-path); overrides genome

gene_anno.comment: gene annotation GTF/GFF3 for TSSe and gene activity (input-path); null skips them with a gap message rather than a slow ~50MB download

genome_fasta.comment: genome FASTA for motif enrichment / TF binding (input-path); null skips motif with a gap message rather than a slow ~845MB download

blacklist.comment: blacklist BED (input-path); null uses the shipped ENCODE blacklist for hg38/mm10, else none

motif_db.comment: motif database .meme (input-path); null uses snapatac2 cis_bp (a download) when motif runs

is_paired.comment: fragments are paired-end; 10x ATAC is paired

min_num_fragments.comment: minimum fragments per barcode at import; below this a barcode is dropped as an empty droplet

bin_size.comment: tile matrix bin size in bp; tiles are the genome-wide binning used for initial clustering, peaks are the called open-chromatin regions

n_features.comment: number of tiles/peaks to select for the spectral embedding; select_features removes uninformative bins

min_counts.comment: minimum fragments per cell for filter_cells; read the n_fragment distribution before choosing

min_tsse.comment: minimum TSS enrichment for filter_cells; null disables the gate (TSSe needs gene_anno). Read the tsse distribution before choosing

max_counts.comment: maximum fragments per cell; null disables the upper gate (a high shoulder can be doublets)

max_tsse.comment: maximum TSS enrichment; null disables the upper gate

doublet_filter.comment: run scrublet on the selected features and filter predicted doublets

doublet_threshold.comment: scrublet doublet probability threshold for filter_doublets

expected_doublet_rate.comment: expected doublet rate for scrublet; scales with loaded cell number

n_comps.comment: spectral embedding components (LSI-like diffusion map on the tile/peak graph)

n_neighbors.comment: neighbors for the kNN graph built on X_spectral

resolution.comment: Leiden clustering resolution; a list sweeps several resolutions to compare granularity

run_umap.comment: compute the UMAP embedding on X_spectral

seed.comment: random seed so spectral, clustering and embedding repeat exactly (snapatac2 default 0)

group_by.comment: obs column defining the clusters for peak calling, markers and annotation

peak_qvalue.comment: MACS3 q-value cutoff for per-cluster peak calling

peak_half_width.comment: half-width in bp to extend each summit before merging peaks into a non-overlapping set

call_broad_peaks.comment: call broad peaks (histone marks); ATAC open chromatin uses narrow peaks

marker_pvalue.comment: p-value cutoff for marker_regions per cluster

diff_min_log_fc.comment: minimum log fold change for diff_test differential accessibility

diff_min_pct.comment: minimum fraction of cells with accessibility for a region to enter diff_test

run_diff.comment: run pairwise cluster-vs-cluster diff_test (O(clusters^2), slow); marker_regions is always cluster-vs-rest

gene_upstream.comment: promoter upstream bp included in the gene activity matrix

gene_body.comment: include the gene body in gene activity; gene activity is a proxy for expression, not RNA

reference_path.comment: scRNA reference .h5ad for label transfer (input-path); null skips transfer. The reference comes from the single-cell plugin

reference_label_key.comment: obs column in the scRNA reference naming cell types

label_column.comment: obs column written with the cell-type labels

panel_path.comment: marker panel JSON (cell type -> gene symbols) for gene-activity scoring (input-path)

mapping_path.comment: cluster -> label JSON overriding panel scores (input-path)

min_score.comment: minimum panel score to accept a label; below it a cluster stays unassigned

motif_pvalue.comment: p-value cutoff for motif enrichment / TF binding scanning

motif_method.comment: motif enrichment test: binomial or hypergeometric

batch_column.comment: obs column naming each cell's sample/batch for integration; the sample is the experimental unit

integrate_method.comment: batch integration on X_spectral: harmony, scanorama or mnc

figures_dir.comment: directory for the HTML copies of every plotly figure

tables_dir.comment: directory for per-cluster marker region tables

plot_tag.comment: suffix for the QC plots; the filter pass re-tags them after

static_png.comment: also write a PNG via kaleido (needs a chrome backend); the interactive HTML is always written

quantiles.comment: distribution quantiles reported for each QC metric

n_jobs.comment: worker processes; keep 1 for reproducibility and small data, raise for large fragment files

meta_path.comment: optional barcode metadata TSV/CSV (for peak matrix TSV/CSV runs)

motif_matches.comment: optional peak x TF binary/weight matrix TSV/CSV for chromVAR tf-deviation

peak_gc.comment: optional peak GC fraction TSV/CSV (chromVAR 5x5 GC+accessibility matching)

n_background.comment: matched background peak iterations per TF for chromVAR deviation z-scores

tfdev_output.comment: output TSV path for per-cell TF motif deviation z-scores

rna_input.comment: paired or cluster-matched scRNA matrix (.h5ad or gene x cell TSV/CSV) for peak2gene linkage

rna_meta.comment: optional scRNA cell metadata TSV/CSV (needed for cluster-level pairing without shared barcodes)

gene_tss.comment: gene TSS coordinates TSV/BED (gene, chrom, tss); overrides gene_anno for peak2gene

peak2gene_max_dist.comment: maximum distance (bp) from gene TSS for cis peak2gene correlation

peak2gene_n_null.comment: trans-chromosome random background pairs for peak2gene empirical FDR

peak2gene_output.comment: output TSV path for significant cis peak-to-gene links

steps.title: Build the tile matrix and select features
Find marker regions and differential accessibility

1.title: Module 01 — scATAC QC
1.intro:
Quality control on raw fragments: per-cell fragment count, duplication and mitochondrial
fraction, fragment size distribution, and TSS enrichment when a gene annotation is supplied.
Threshold filtering plus scrublet doublet removal, with a report of what each gate removed.
Reads a fragments.tsv.gz, a BAM, a saved .h5ad or a 10x peak matrix.

Original distillation of the snapatac2 documentation (MIT); the code is original to this plugin.

2.title: Module 02 — Preprocess and cluster
2.intro:
The QC chain plus a genome-wide tile matrix, feature selection, spectral embedding (the
scATAC analogue of LSI/PCA), a kNN graph, Leiden clustering and UMAP. Tiles are used for
clustering because they cover the genome uniformly; called peaks come later for differential
accessibility.

Original distillation of the snapatac2 documentation (MIT).

3.title: Module 03 — Peaks and marker regions
3.intro:
The clustered chain plus per-cluster MACS3 peak calling, a merged non-overlapping peak set,
a peak-count matrix and per-cluster marker regions (cluster-vs-rest differential accessibility).
Pairwise cluster-vs-cluster diff_test is opt-in via run_diff because it is O(clusters^2). This
is where open-chromatin regions become the features of record for downstream comparison.

Original distillation of the snapatac2 documentation (MIT).

4.title: Module 04 — Gene activity and annotation
4.intro:
The clustered chain plus a gene activity matrix (accessibility aggregated over gene bodies
and promoters) and cell-type annotation, either by scoring a marker panel on gene activity or
by transferring labels from a scRNA reference. Gene activity is a proxy for expression, not
RNA; it needs a gene annotation.

Original distillation of the snapatac2 documentation (MIT).

5.title: Module 05 — Motif and integration
5.intro:
The annotated chain plus motif enrichment on per-cluster marker regions (which TF motifs
are over-represented in each cluster's open chromatin) and sample integration with Harmony on
the spectral embedding. Motif enrichment needs a genome FASTA and a motif database; without
them the cell reports the gap and continues.

Original distillation of the snapatac2 documentation (MIT).

6.title: Module 06 — Full scATAC chain
6.intro:
Every capability in order: QC, tile matrix, spectral embedding, clustering, per-cluster
peaks, marker regions, gene activity, annotation, motif enrichment and sample integration.
Steps that need a missing genome resource, reference or package report the gap and continue.

Original distillation of the snapatac2 documentation (MIT).

7.title: Module 07 — TF motif deviations and Peak-to-Gene linkage
7.intro:
Regulatory chromatin interpretation beyond cluster-level motif enrichment: computes
GC-matched chromVAR per-cell TF motif deviation z-scores and cis Peak-to-Gene enhancer
correlations against paired scRNA expression with trans-chromosome empirical FDR.
